name: Vincent Sitzmann
headline: Assistant Professor @ MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL).
summary:
I am a computer vision researcher with a focus on 3d scene representations. Specifically, I am researching how we can distill pictures of a scene into a representation that is accessible to machine learning algorithms, to solve problems such as scene reconstruction, novel view synthesis, scene understanding, etc. My day-to-day tools are deep learning, optimization, as well as multi-view and projective geometry.

In another line of research, I am interested in end-to-end optimization of cameras for the joint design of algorithms and hardware for true task-specific sensors.

positions.title: Assistant Professor
positions.description: I am an Assistant Professor at MIT CSAIL, where I am leading the Scene Representation Group (scenerepresentations.com). My group investigates neural scene representations - the way neural networks learn to represent information on our world. Our goal is to allow independent agents to reason about our world given visual observations, such as inferring a complete model of a scene with information on geometry, material, lighting etc. from only few observations, and then plan and execute actions in the scene, a task that is simple for humans, but remains a significant challenge for AI.
